text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx spike detected in model-runner-prod (us-east-1). 15m error rate 12% (threshold 5%). Affected route: /v1/generate (model service). Escalation: P1. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/model-runtime-5xx

sara: ack — I'm oncall. looking now. @kai can you grab the runner logs for runner-gpu-3 and the delivery gateway?

kai: pulling logs. immediate symptoms: repeated segfaults and CUDA OOMs from model v2.1.3 process. attaching recent tail: 
```
[2026-02-14T02:10:12Z] runner[v2.1.3] ERROR: runtime: segfault at 0x7f3a8c...
signal 11 (SIGSEGV) code=1 pc=0x7f3a8c...
[2026-02-14T02:10:12Z] kernel: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-02-14T02:10:12Z] runner[v2.1.3] INFO: crash reporter saved core to /var/crash/runner-1234.core
```

mike: noting customers are hitting 502/504. I'm going to flip traffic to fallback model variant v2.0.9 now (no config change required on client). doing a weighted route shift (50% -> 100% if healthy).

sara: do it. also follow runbook: if segfaults + OOM, cordon the node and restart the runner service after capturing core. @pat can you cordon runner-gpu-3 and restart?

pat: cordoning node and draining. 
```bash
kubectl cordon runner-gpu-3.us-east-1
kubectl drain runner-gpu-3.us-east-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
systemctl restart redwood-runner
```
Pat: core dump uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/1769254321/runner-1234.core

kai: starting heap/profile capture from the core and the process pid snapshot. Also enabling extra runtime debug logs at level=debug for the model runtime.

ryan: pushing emergency config change to runtime: reduce `max_batch_size` from 16 -> 8 and `max_prefill_seq_len` from 2048 -> 1024 to reduce memory pressure. deploying via configmap patch. rolling restart of the service for the cluster. command: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runner-config --patch '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8","max_prefill_seq_len":"1024"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runner-deployment
```

eng-sre-bot: Automated mitigation policy triggered: route fallback to v2.0.9 confirmed, cluster autoscaler temporarily increased min replicas by +2. Suppressing duplicate alerts for 15m.

support-agent: Customer-facing update: CS notified customers with active incidents (Customer A, Customer B) and posted interim advisory. CS ticket: #INC-8421.

sara: monitoring metrics now. initial signal: 5xx rate down to ~6.2% after route shift and restart, p95 latency normalizing. still seeing sporadic segfaults from 1 node before drain.

kai: captured stack traces, keys: 
```
#0 0x7f3a8c... in attention_kernel::compute(...)
#1 0x7f3b2d... in kv_cache::append(...)
#2 0x55a1f3... in runner::infer
```
plus repeated `cudaMalloc` failures when sequence length > 1500 tokens.

mike: good call on fallback. holding rollout of v2.1.3 for now. we'll need to test next patch with smaller batch and kernel sanity checks.

ryan: can we temporarily enable per-request fallback if runtime reports high mem usage? we have a feature flag `runtime.degrade_to_fallback_on_mem` — I can toggle to true for prod.

sara: toggle it. do it and confirm traffic policy.

ryan: toggled `runtime.degrade_to_fallback_on_mem=true` for prod. policy in place: if runtime reports >85% GPU mem and queue length high, send that request to fallback variant.

eng-sre-bot: Feature flag change recorded: runtime.degrade_to_fallback_on_mem=true by ryan at 02:29 UTC.

sara: quick status update for handoff: mitigations performed: 1) immediate weighted route fallback to v2.0.9, 2) cordoned and restarted runner-gpu-3, 3) reduced max_batch_size and prefill len to reduce mem pressure, 4) autoscaler bumped +2, 5) feature flag enabled to degrade to fallback on mem pressure, 6) core dump + profiles uploaded for postmortem. Customer teams notified.

kai: uploading logs + traces: https://s3.redwood/1769254321/artifacts.zip (profiles, core dumps, kernel logs, stack traces).

mike: seeing error rate down to 2.1% over last 5m. p95 latency back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated for now.

sara: agreed. we'll keep monitoring for 60 minutes. if stable, we'll close the page and open follow-up ticket for postmortem and release-block on v2.1.3 until kernel validated.

pat: one more note — node had ~3.6GB of GPU fragmentation reported by nvidia-smi prior to crash; likely attention kernel change caused sudden OOM during long sequences.

ryan: action items: (1) revert traffic permanent to v2.0.9 until v2.1.3 is validated; (2) add regression test covering long sequence scenarios; (3) add alert for cudaMalloc error spikes; (4) postmortem owner = sara.

eng-sre-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Auto-close disabled; manual close required.

sara: handoff notes for night oncall (ryan): will pass to you in 30m if still stable. summary for handoff: suspected runtime OOM/segfault in model v2.1.3 under long sequences causing 5xx spike; mitigations applied; artifacts uploaded; CS alerted. Please monitor error rate and confirm no regression after config changes.

ryan: taking handoff. I'll monitor for next 2 hours. thanks.

sara: closing real-time coordination. I'll file the postmortem template and link artifacts: https://redwood/pm/1769254321. postmortem checklist items assigned.

mike: thumbs up. great teamwork. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Notification: page acknowledged and mitigations in progress. Remember to run the post-incident runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/oncall-post-incident
